label: Early original-phase step (t=1-4) inputting b/s/p/z/k/j/a/f/g after a prefix of c/h/2/x/0/e/w/d/l/v
explanation: Most activation mass (90%) is in the original phase at steps 1-4 (t=2 alone has 40%). It never fires at t=0 and almost never at the delimiter. The strongest driver is the current input: b (24% firing rate), then s, p, z, k, j, and more weakly a, f, g. Magnitude also goes up when the earlier tokens come from c/h/2/x/0/e/w/d/l/v. The top activations (~0.4) are all 'b' at t=2-3 after a prefix like 'x h c', 'h c w' or '2 h w'. The neuron behaves like an additive score (early position + current-token weight + prefix-token weights), so boolean rules top out near F1 0.5. The simpler rule 'original t in 1-3 and input in {b,s,p,z,k,j}' gets dev F1 0.46 and mass recall 0.58. Weak, diffuse firing in the copy phase (~10% of mass, mostly when outputting d/x/c/2/h) is not captured. It rarely fires on repeated tokens (in_first=0) or late original positions (t>=5).
